card: Adds an upstream patch for python-oscrypto to the Guix build configuration to fix a ZeroDivisionError during guix-codesign. When substitutes are disabled, building oscrypto from source fails on OpenSSL 3.5.5 (bumped in #36233) because its PBKDF2 benchmark finishes in under one millisecond and truncates to zero before division. This unblocks release signers and developers compiling guix-codesign from source without substitutes.
evidence: PR description: 'With substitutes disabled, guix-codesign can fail when building oscrypto 1.3.0. The test_dump_private test raises ZeroDivisionError.'
problem: When building `guix-codesign` without pre-built substitutes, building `oscrypto` 1.3.0 fails during its `test_dump_private` test. OpenSSL 3.5.5 (introduced by the Guix time-machine bump in #36233) runs PBKDF2 fast enough to finish under one millisecond, which oscrypto truncates to zero before dividing by elapsed time.

risk.why: An error in the patch would only break the Guix build for code-signing tools when building without substitutes.

scope_notes: Adds an upstream patch file under contrib/guix/patches and updates the Guix manifest to apply it.
summary: Adds an upstream backport patch to `contrib/guix/patches` for the `oscrypto` package used in code signing. The patch resolves a `ZeroDivisionError` in oscrypto's test suite when benchmarking PBKDF2 under OpenSSL 3.5.5.
uncertainties: Diff was omitted from the prompt, although the change is narrowly described as adding an upstream patch file.
